$comment: brief2dev transplant-bundle receipt — Inventory SSOT for bundles transplanted into this project. role=managed files are brief2dev code: sha256 is the base a re-transplant merges local edits against (unchanged upstream → kept, otherwise 3-way merged; overlapping edits are left for a hand merge). Fixes that apply to every project belong in brief2dev source. role=customizable files are edited by this project and preserved during re-transplants.

git-worktree-isolation.title: Git/Worktree Isolation + AI Safety Git Guards + Worktree Creation Tools (Multi-CLI)

target_notes.note: The `.brief2dev/system` symlink created by worktree-init.mjs exists for brief2dev cross-idea SSOT sharing. When the target has no `.brief2dev/system`, init handles it gracefully (missing main system dir branch) — only PLAN.md auto-creation is effective there and the symlink step is a no-op. Single-clone projects that do not need worktree isolation can use the guard hooks alone.

worktree-policy.json is transplanted by remapping the generic template (data/registry/transplant-templates/worktree-policy.generic.json) to .claude/config/worktree-policy.json — only ecosystem-neutral git-ignored outputs (.tmp/.cache/dist/build/node_modules/target/.next, etc.) plus .claude/settings.json (hook-registration codegen special case, a git-tracked exception) are Tier 1. brief2dev-specific paths (.brief2dev/output) are not included. `.claude/config/**` (including the policy file itself) is Tier 3 — the same paradigm as brief2dev's own policy (corrected 2026-07-01; the earlier version omitted settings.json, a self-lock gap that blocked hook-registration edits right after transplanting). The target may add or remove tier1 patterns for its own git-ignored directories (optional). Denying edits to tracked files (README.md, etc.) on main is the intended behavior of the worktree paradigm — if isolation is not wanted, do not register worktree-policy-guard.

Two opt-in Bash policies in .claude/config/worktree-policy.json (added 2026-09-23, upstreamed from a target that had hard-coded them into the guards): `trunk_bash_allowlist` {enabled, patterns[]} and `session_owner_scope: "all_bash"`. Exact semantics are in the generic template (trunk_bash_allowlist.description, _adapt.session_owner_scope) and the headers of worktree-policy-guard.mjs / worktree-session-owner-guard.mjs / bash-segments.mjs. Both default off, and a target without the keys behaves exactly as before. Claude Code wiring stays narrow by default (no worktree-policy-guard on Bash, `if: Bash(git *)` on the session-owner Bash entry) because each extra Bash hook is a node process per Bash call (~55 ms measured 2026-09-23). Opting in under Claude Code therefore also means editing the target's .claude/settings.json: add worktree-policy-guard.mjs to PreToolUse Bash without `if`, and drop the `if` from worktree-session-owner-guard.mjs. Re-transplant keeps both (merge dedupes by command). Codex/Antigravity registrations run both guards on every Bash call already (one extra dispatch per Bash call for worktree-policy-guard, returning after one JSON read when not opted in).

Opt-in `enforce_worktree_all_branches: true` in .claude/config/worktree-policy.json (added 2026-09-23, upstreamed from a git-flow target that had forked commit-guard / worktree-policy-guard / trunk-start-warning for it): a non-worktree checkout on any branch (develop, release/*) except escape-hatch branches (hotfix/*) is treated like trunk by all four trunk consumers; worktrees must live under .worktrees/ for the guards to recognise them. The key is read in one place, .cli/lib/trunk-branch.mjs#enforcesWorktreeOnAllBranches; exact per-guard effects are in the generic template's _adapt.enforce_worktree_all_branches. Default false: a target without the key behaves exactly as before. No settings.json change is needed. Same change: trunk-start-warning no longer warns when the session cwd is inside a linked worktree (checked with git rev-parse --git-dir vs --git-common-dir).

Opt-out `trunk_ref_guard: false` in .claude/config/worktree-policy.json (added 2026-10-01): the git-level trunk guard passes every ref update. Use it only where an AI-run local merge into trunk is the documented landing (no remote, so /create-pr and its lease never run) — otherwise the guard blocks that landing. Only a JSON false opts out; a missing key keeps the guard on. The policy file is customizable, so the opt-out survives re-transplanting. Semantics: generic template _adapt.trunk_ref_guard.

worktree-new.mjs auto-detects the base branch (origin/HEAD → main → master), and in a purely local repo without an origin remote it skips fetch/ff and creates the worktree from the local <base> — external projects defaulting to master or without a remote work unmodified.

Trunk (protected) branch SSOT (defect fixed 2026-08-01): which branches count as "no direct work" is decided by one transitively collected module, .cli/lib/trunk-branch.mjs, shared by commit-guard / worktree-policy-guard / worktree-shipping-guard / trunk-start-warning. The default is both main and master, so master-default projects work with no configuration. If the default branch has another name (trunk / develop / release, etc.), list it in the protected_branches array of .claude/config/worktree-policy.json (a customizable file transplanted via extra_files — edits survive re-transplantation). Earlier versions hardcoded 'main' in commit-guard and worktree-shipping-guard only, so on master-default targets file-edit blocking and session warnings worked while **direct trunk commits silently got through** and the trunk repo itself was treated as a ship candidate — targets transplanted from an old receipt are fixed by re-transplanting.
trunk-start-warning performs SessionStart context injection (warns to create a worktree when entering main directly), preventing accidental direct commits on trunk branches.

Customization protection on re-transplant (added 2026-07-01): files transplanted as extra_files, such as worktree-policy.json, are designed to be edited directly by the target after transplanting (adding/removing tier1 patterns). Re-running the same bundle SKIPs extra_files that already exist in the target with different content, preserving customizations (`--force` overwrites). entry_hooks/entry_scripts/CLI registration JSON are mechanism code maintained by brief2dev, so they are not protected and are always refreshed on re-transplant. Root cause: without this safeguard a re-transplant could silently revert the target's customizations to generic defaults.

PLAN.md checkboxes → human review → approval marker procedure (added 2026-07-02): mark-pre-ship-confirmed.mjs (creates the approval marker) and pre-ship-review-guard.mjs (PreToolUse Bash guard checking marker freshness) are transplanted, so the target also enforces review-panel approval before any `ship-*` command. The step sequence comes from lib/pre-ship-steps.mjs (machine steps first, human steps last), run through the pre-ship-steps.mjs CLI. .claude/config/approval-policy.json is deliberately not shipped: without it every diff is T2, so the `approval` step always waits for a human and approval-trust.mjs reports the file as missing — add a policy only to opt into auto-approval. The remaining libs (PLAN template, ship report, section renderer, quality-gate labels/PROOF, PLAN path/status) are collected by BFS as well.

Review panel section customization (added 2026-07-02, handoff seed added 2026-07-14): worktree-plan-sections.json (PLAN.md default-section seed — DEFAULT_PLAN_SECTIONS is the SSOT), worktree-handoff-sections.json (handoff.md RETURN contract seed — DEFAULT_HANDOFF_SECTIONS is the SSOT), and pre-ship-review-panel-sections.json (approval panel — DEFAULT_REVIEW_SECTIONS is the SSOT) are transplanted as directly editable seeds via extra_files — heading text, section count, checklist items and table columns can all be changed freely. The `sections` schema of the three JSONs is exactly the five block types (static/checklist_group/field_list/fenced_block/table) interpreted by section-template-renderer.mjs#renderTemplateFromSections. The plan and handoff JSONs are not read by brief2dev (option C — the live path uses the DEFAULT_PLAN_SECTIONS/DEFAULT_HANDOFF_SECTIONS JS constants): to use them, wire worktree-init.mjs to pass them as `options.sections`, or replace the constants in the transplanted worktree-plan-template.mjs. The panel JSON is read on the live path since 2026-09-23 once it opts in with `"override": true` — the seed ships false, so seeds already copied into targets stay inert instead of freezing stale sections (.cli/lib/worktree-ship-report.mjs#loadReviewPanelConfig, used by pre-ship-review-guard, worktree-shipping-guard, the pre-ship step runner and the ship-worktree completion report) and additionally accepts `locale`, `labels` (DEFAULT_REPORT_LABELS keys), `approval_choices` and `line_budget` — so a target localizes or condenses the panel, completion report and approval choices by editing that file instead of the managed .mjs files; malformed keys fall back to the built-in English. The ship deck is localized separately through the project-owned `.claude/reach-map.json` (`locale` selects ship-deck-render.mjs#DECK_LABELS; `tiers.<id>.{label,short,means}` re-words reach tiers).

Non-customizable files (added 2026-07-02, worktree-quality-gate.mjs added 2026-07-14): quality-gate-labels.mjs / worktree-plan-status.mjs / worktree-quality-gate.mjs are brief2dev-maintained code collected by BFS as transitive dependencies of entry_hooks/entry_scripts — they are not extra_files, so they carry no customizable flag and are always overwritten with the latest version on re-transplant (if the target edited these three files directly, back them up before re-transplanting).

ops.mjs depends on GitHub Flow (added 2026-07-02, resolved 2026-07-03 by transplanting create-pr): previously the automation after the approval marker — push/PR/squash-merge (`/create-pr` skill, `.claude/scripts/create-pr/ops.mjs`) — was not part of this bundle. Since 2026-07-03 the `create-pr` skill itself is transplanted via entry_skills: commit-guard/destructive-git-guard/worktree-session-owner-guard/worktree-shipping-guard reference the `.tmp/create-pr-active` carve-out marker (written by `ops.mjs` init/isolate/commit/ship-feature; removed by finalize and by init's cleanup of an abandoned session; cleanup-worktree does not touch it) and the `/create-pr ship-worktree` guidance text directly in code, so without create-pr the only release path for these hooks did not exist in the target (pre-ship-review-guard deliberately ignores the marker — it guards the ship command itself) (entry_scripts also includes `create-pr/ops.mjs` — join() accepts sub-paths as-is, so no schema/code change was needed). Remaining limit: if the target is not on GitHub or uses a different PR workflow, the logic depending on the `gh` CLI must be reimplemented.

create-pr/config.json genericized (added 2026-07-03): `.claude/skills/create-pr/config.json` holds brief2dev's own values (e.g. a specific GitHub account) and must not be transplanted as-is — an extra_files remap installs `data/registry/transplant-templates/create-pr-config.generic.json` instead (only `base_branch: "main"`, no `github_account`). `github_account` is an optional field needed only when several GitHub accounts are logged in to the `gh` CLI on one machine (multi-account disambiguation) — with a single account, omitting it uses `gh`'s default login, so the template leaves it out. Add it to `config.json` in the target if needed. When entry_skills (whole-directory copy) and extra_files (generic remap) target the same path, extra_files always wins (Map insertion order by destRel in `planTransplant`).

Soft references in create-pr SKILL.md (added 2026-07-03): create-pr SKILL.md/MANIFEST.json mentions /pre-ship-quality-advisor, code-standards-aligner, final-review, make q.ci-mirror, etc., but these are recommendations or optional Makefile targets — not included in this bundle (hard runtime dependencies only). The core create-pr flow (init/isolate/commit/ship-feature/finalize/verify-plan/ship-worktree/cleanup-worktree) operates normally without them (ops.mjs#cmdInit checks make -n q.ci-mirror first and skips the gate if absent).

quality-gate.json PROOF persistence (added 2026-07-14, teamwork-preview transplant Phase 2): When review/gate results (verdict go|no_go + gates[]{name,status,command,detail,finding}) are recorded to worktree mailbox (.tmp/worktree-<safeBranch>/quality-gate.json) via record-quality-gate.mjs, mark-pre-ship-confirmed.mjs rejects creating approval markers if verdict=no_go (--force override available). Opt-in by presence — target projects not recording PROOF automatically skip checks without changes to marker procedures. Schema contract SSOT is transitively collected worktree-quality-gate.mjs.

v1.2: mark-pre-ship-confirmed.mjs re-runs the Task Passport acceptance[] (file_exists | grep | command) recorded by task-interpretation.mjs record --acceptance and rejects the ship on failure. Without a passport or acceptance the gate skips with a note (fail-open) — the passport is written by task-context-injector (not in this bundle) or manually via task-interpretation.mjs record.

feature-delivery-core.title: SPEC Delivery Core (Architect → SPEC → UI Approval → Implementation → Wiring → Status Sync, Excluding Orchestrators)

target_notes.note: The orchestrator feature-pilot is intentionally excluded — the skills run as a manual pipeline, each invoked on its own trigger ('update the SPEC', 'verify integration', 'check the wireframe', etc.). To add feature-pilot, layer the feature-orchestration bundle (added 2026-07-12) on top after this one — it verifies its prerequisites (this bundle among four) via requires_bundles, and its pf-runtime-prereqs note covers the POF-003 (pre-quality-gate) / PF-008 (worktree) / PF-010 (ownership index) / Makefile q.check prerequisites.

feature-doctor (.quality/scripts/feature_doctor.py) and spec-validator (scripts/validate.py + jsonschema) are excluded because they need a Python runtime plus pip dependencies. SPEC generation in feature-spec-generator works without them; if SPEC schema validation is needed, install python3 + pip install jsonschema in the target and transplant spec-validator separately (docs/_templates/schemas/*.schema.json must come along).

quality-gate-core.title: Quality Gate Core (Quality Check → Verification Loop → Standards Alignment → Pre-Ship Advisor → Final Review, Excluding Orchestrators)

target_notes.note: (2026-08-05: Copy mode automatically derives q.check/q.fix bridge recipes from scripts[typecheck/lint/test/build] in target package.json — including stamp touch. Only when zero scripts can be derived does the manual requirement below remain, in which case report.wiring.readiness.unmet explicitly reports it.) pre-quality-gate requires q.check (mandatory) / q.fix / q.secrets / q.deps-audit targets in the target project's own Makefile to operate (running Makefile targets is the skill's purpose). If absent, define equivalent targets in Makefile (consolidating lint+test+build) or omit pre-quality-gate during transplant. The remaining 4 skills are Makefile-independent: verification-loop/final-review have built-in platform fallback tables when project-config.json is absent; code-standards-aligner/pre-ship-quality-advisor are self-detecting (session modified files, adjacent code patterns, git diff --stat) with zero prerequisites.

References in final-review references/final-review-protocol-details.md mention make q.lint/q.test/q.check-architecture, but these are deep-reference examples, not contracts of the main body — SKILL.md dynamically resolves commands via project-config.json. Harmless if target lacks those make targets. Mentions of .brief2dev/ in references/pr-review-protocol.md are also provenance metadata and checklist examples, unrelated to runtime.

pre-ship-quality-advisor detects CLI via $CLAUDECODE, recommending /code-review in Claude Code and code-standards-aligner in other CLIs — because the fallback target is included in this bundle, routing resolves internally within the bundle. Mention of /create-pr ship-worktree is a soft trigger description, not a hard dependency (works without git-worktree-isolation bundle).

feature-orchestration.title: Feature Development Full Orchestration (feature-pilot Single Entrypoint + Implementation Plan Authoring + Derived Code Ownership Index)

target_notes.note: Of feature-pilot's 16 calls, only research-pilot / priority-analyzer lie outside this bundle + prerequisite bundles, both declared as optional_skills since SKILL.md specifies 'SKIP if absent'. The core delivery loop (task classification -> SPEC -> implementation -> wiring -> status sync -> QA -> final review) completes with prerequisite bundles. **Previous revision of this note (prior to 2026-08-17) described 11 uncovered items as 'discovery/design extension routing targets', which was untrue** — those 11 were never named anywhere in feature-pilot instructions and could never trigger routing (12 discrepancies with invocation rules table); even if placed in targets, feature-pilot had no way to call them. Corrected declarations to actual call set. Recurrence prevented by D1 in skill-consistency-check.

scripts/validate_spec.py in feature-pilot is an optional wrapper invoking validate.py of python3 + spec-validator skill (excluded from feature-delivery-core due to python jsonschema dependency) via subprocess — if python3/spec-validator is absent in target, only SPEC placeholder validation fails/skips while core loop remains intact. Because it is a script explicitly called by AI per SKILL.md instructions rather than a hook, there is no fail-closed risk (reason for polyglot entry hook prohibition).

The 3 prerequisites for feature-pilot Pre/Post-flight require target environment preparation — (1) PF-000: target root project-config.json (paths/commands SSOT). If absent, reported by report.wiring.readiness.unmet — paths/conventions are assumptions of target structure, so not auto-generated. Generation recommended (identical schema to ecosystem-adapter Phase 2 output). (2) PF-008: worktree creation + PLAN.md initialization — companion transplant of git-worktree-isolation bundle recommended (not required — non-worktree projects replace this check with own branch conventions). (3) POF-003: pre-quality-gate is satisfied by quality-gate-core, but requires Makefile q.check target per that bundle's target-makefile-q-family-required note.

generate-code-ownership-index.mjs is an index derived from project-config.json/docs/features/domain-map.json/feature CONTEXT.json/SPEC documents (not a new SSOT) — joins with docs/_templates conventions transplanted by feature-delivery-core. In initial states without source files, outputs an empty candidate index without failing.

target_notes.note: Each skill ends with an "In This Repository" section that names the repo entry points it defers to (worktree creation, PLAN.md location, quality gate command, ship command).
